action_items: NOTE (already fixed by tester): server.py line 312 — ApprovalType Literal was missing 'advance_request' and 'advance_settlement' although APPROVAL_TYPE_COLL (line 318) and _approval_link (line 4214) already had them. This caused POST /api/approval-chains (422 literal_error) and POST /api/approvals/act (422) to reject the new type, blocking end-to-end approval flow. Fix applied in this iteration.
MINOR: GET /api/transactions returns 500 for admin — pre-existing (predates iter-38). Please investigate independently; not blocking the Advance module.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:312 ApprovalType Literal — MUST stay in sync with APPROVAL_TYPE_COLL keys (line 318). This drift bit us here. Consider deriving ApprovalType from the dict keys via `Literal[*APPROVAL_TYPE_COLL.keys()]` (Python 3.11+) or using a single source of truth to prevent future omissions.

server.py:9138 create_advance_request — good: uses uuid.uuid4() id, atomically generates ADV-YY-NNNN via _next_advance_no, populates employee_* from linked staff (falls back to user name/email). chain snapshot attached via existing helper. Sends notifications to first-step approvers, correctly skipping self-notify.

server.py:9090/9107 _next_advance_no & _next_voucher_no — sequential regex-then-parse-tail-int is fine for low-volume; race window exists under concurrent inserts (no unique index). Consider a counters collection with $inc for atomic sequencing — MINOR follow-up.
server.py:9123 _advance_scope_filter — clean role-based visibility. Note: senior_manager/manager see EVERYTHING (matches spec) but this bypasses partner/center scope; confirm this matches org policy.

server.py:9234 get_advance_request — non-owner access-check reduces via _advance_scope_filter but the all-key conjunction reads oddly: `all(row.get(k) in ...)`. For `center_id: {'$in': [...]}` scope it's OK; but if a future scope has multiple keys OR partner_id=None, this may over-restrict. Consider re-fetching via query rather than manual field-matching.

server.py:9265 release_advance — good gating (require_role admin/accountant), status must be 'approved', already-released check via released_at. Linked transaction row uses status='posted' and category='advance' which is queryable via advance_request_id. Balance_amount initialised to paid_amount — correct groundwork for Phase 2 adjustment.

server.py:9339 cancel_advance_request — 204 correctly, but the request spec mentions 'admin can cancel anything' — currently code allows admin to cancel even released/adjusting/settled, which may not be desirable for released rows since it doesn't reverse the linked transaction. Consider soft-guard against cancelling released rows without also reversing the txn. Not tested this iteration.

Advances.jsx — all requested data-testids present and wired. Release paid-by dropdown lists ALL users (196 in test env) which is noisy; consider narrowing to admins/accountants or role='paying_role' — MINOR UX.

PATCH advance-requests uses AdvanceRequestIn which is not partial (all required fields marked). model_dump(exclude_unset=True) partially rescues this, but if client omits `purpose` the patch route will still reject at validation (min_length=2 on purpose). Consider a separate AdvanceRequestPatchIn with all optional fields — MINOR.
